summary: This standards-track RFC defines how to carry HEVC video, also known as H.265, in RTP packets. It allows one or more units of the encoded video to be packetized for transmission.

plainLanguage.summary: A video is chopped into little packets, and this explains how to pack and label H.265 video so it can be sent over a network and rebuilt.

subtitle: How H.265 video is split into NAL units and carried inside RTP packets, with aggregation, fragmentation and SDP signaling.

tldr.problem: HEVC (H.265) produces a stream of small and large coded units, and RTP packets must fit the network MTU and still let a receiver recover the units in decoding order.
tldr.mechanism: The RTP payload carries NAL units in four structures: a single NAL unit packet, an aggregation packet (type 48), a fragmentation unit (type 49) and a PACI packet (type 50). Media type parameters describe the stream in SDP.
tldr.outcome: Senders and receivers can stream HEVC over one or several RTP streams, with optional interleaving and temporal scalability control. It follows the design of the H.264 and SVC payload formats.

today: RFC 7798 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2016, and the metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It remains the definition of the HEVC RTP payload format.

sections.title: Carrying HEVC over RTP
sections.content:
High Efficiency Video Coding is published as ITU-T Recommendation H.265 and ISO/IEC 23008-2. This RFC defines how its coded data is carried over RTP (RFC 3550). It shares its basic design with the RTP payload formats of RFC 6184 (H.264) and RFC 6190, a conscious choice since RFC 6184 is widely deployed. Mechanisms from RFC 6190 were included because HEVC version 1 supports temporal scalability.

Like H.264, HEVC has a Video Coding Layer and a Network Abstraction Layer (NAL). The NAL packages coded data into NAL units, and the payload format is built around them.

The RFC covers the use of the RTP header, packetization of NAL units with three payload structures plus the PACI extension mechanism, transmission in a single RTP stream or several (interleaved or not), media type parameters for SDP, and a header extension for temporal scalability.
sections.plainLanguage: The video is already cut into labeled chunks. This document says how to put those chunks into envelopes the network can carry and how to read the labels again.

sections.title: The NAL Unit Header and RTP Header Rules
sections.content:
An HEVC NAL unit starts with a two-byte header: F (1 bit, forbidden zero bit), Type (6 bits), LayerId (6 bits) and TID (3 bits, the temporal identifier plus 1). A TID of 0 is illegal. Types below 32 are VCL NAL units, which carry coded video; the rest are non-VCL.

The payload format uses the RTP header as follows:

  • The marker bit is set on the last packet of an access unit in the RTP stream.
  • The payload type is assigned outside this document, by the profile or dynamically.
  • The timestamp is the sampling time of the content and a 90 kHz clock rate MUST be used. NAL units without timing of their own, such as parameter sets and SEI, take the timestamp of their access unit.
  • Receivers MUST use the RTP timestamp for display, even if picture timing SEI messages are present.

The first two bytes of every RTP payload are the payload header, with the same F, Type, LayerId and TID fields. Because a lower TID means a more important packet, more important NAL units MAY be better protected against loss.
sections.plainLanguage: Each chunk carries a tiny label saying what kind it is and how important it is. The envelope also carries a clock reading so the pictures show up at the right moment.

sections.title: The Four Payload Structures
sections.content:
The Type field in the payload header tells the receiver which of four structures a packet uses.

A single NAL unit packet holds exactly one NAL unit. The payload header SHOULD be an exact copy of the NAL unit header, followed by an optional 16-bit DONL field and the NAL unit payload.

An aggregation packet (AP, Type 48) packs two or more NAL units of one access unit, in decoding order, to avoid overhead for small NAL units. Each aggregation unit has a 16-bit size field. APs MUST NOT be nested and MUST NOT contain FUs. The size SHOULD keep the IP packet under the MTU.

A fragmentation unit (FU, Type 49) carries part of one NAL unit. Its one-octet FU header has an S bit (start), an E bit (end) and a 6-bit FuType copied from the original NAL unit type. Fragments MUST be sent consecutively with ascending sequence numbers, S and E MUST NOT both be 1, and an FU payload MUST NOT be empty. If an FU is lost, the receiver SHOULD discard the following FUs of the same NAL unit.

A PACI packet (Type 50) carries a payload header extension structure (PHES) in front of a single NAL unit, FU or AP, so control information sits in an easily reached position. PACIs MUST NOT be fragmented or aggregated.
sections.plainLanguage: Small chunks are bundled in one box. A huge chunk is cut into several boxes marked first, middle and last. A special box can carry an extra note on the outside.

sections.title: Transmission Modes, Ordering and Buffering
sections.content:
An HEVC bitstream can go over a Single RTP stream on a Single media Transport (SRST), Multiple RTP streams over a Single media Transport (MRST), or Multiple RTP streams on Multiple media Transports (MRMT). The tx-mode parameter selects the mode. SRST or MRST SHOULD be used for point-to-point unicast, and MRMT SHOULD be used for multicast where receivers need different operation points. Receivers MUST support all three.

When sprop-max-don-diff is 0 for all streams, NAL units MUST be sent in decoding order. When it is greater than 0, NAL units MAY be sent out of order, and each carries a decoding order number (DONL, plus a DOND field for non-first aggregation units) so the receiver can restore the order. The receiver derives AbsDon from these, and a looping 16-bit comparison handles wrap-around.

The receiver stores NAL units in a de-packetization buffer and releases the one with the smallest AbsDon once an initial-buffering condition is met, based on sprop-max-don-diff or sprop-depack-buf-nalus. NAL-unit-like structures with type values 48 to 63 MUST NOT be passed to the decoder.

Packetization advice: small NAL units SHOULD be aggregated, and a non-VCL NAL unit SHOULD travel with its associated VCL NAL unit when the MTU allows. Exactly one NAL unit in a packet MUST use a single NAL unit packet.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes the boxes arrive in the wrong order, so each carries a number. The receiver waits for a few boxes and then unpacks them in number order.

sections.title: Media Type Parameters and SDP
sections.content:
The RFC registers the media type video/H265. It has no required parameters, and receivers MUST ignore unrecognized ones. Optional parameters describe the stream or the receiver's capability:

  • profile-space, profile-id, tier-flag, level-id, profile-compatibility-indicator and interop-constraints give the profile, tier and level. If absent, profile-space defaults to 0, profile-id to 1 (the Main profile), tier-flag to 0 and level-id to 93 (level 3.1).
  • tx-mode chooses SRST, MRST or MRMT.
  • sprop-max-don-diff and sprop-depack-buf-nalus relate to interleaving and buffering.

These map into SDP (RFC 4566) a=fmtp lines. Section 7.2 covers usage in the offer/answer model, where for example profile-related parameters MUST generally be used symmetrically, and in declarative session descriptions. The long per-parameter definitions are only summarized here.
sections.plainLanguage: Before the video starts, both sides swap a short checklist saying what kind of video they can handle, so they agree on the settings.

sections.title: Feedback Messages for Loss Recovery
sections.content:
The RFC defines how four RTCP feedback messages work with HEVC:

  • Picture Loss Indication (PLI): the sender SHOULD respond by sending an IDR picture and the relevant parameter sets, unless it knows they are not needed.
  • Slice Loss Indication (SLI): reports lost coded tree blocks in raster scan order, with the PictureID set to the 6 least significant bits of PicOrderCntVal.
  • Reference Picture Selection Indication (RPSI): the decoder tells the encoder a good earlier picture to use. Use as a positive acknowledgement is deprecated.
  • Full Intra Request (FIR): on reception, a sender MUST send an IDR picture, plus parameter sets unless the receiver is known to have them.

In all cases the timing and congestion control rules of the underlying feedback RFCs MUST be observed.
sections.plainLanguage: If the picture goes wrong, the receiver can radio back and ask the sender to send a fresh full picture.

sections.title: Security and Congestion Control
sections.content:
The payload format itself adds no security threats beyond those common to RTP, except one HEVC feature. The user data SEI message can carry arbitrary bitstrings, even JavaScript or machine code, so decoders cannot naively trust it. The safest handling is to discard it.

Because compression is end-to-end, encryption has to happen after compression. A decoder can also be overloaded by pathological packets, since H.265 NAL units can affect the decoding of many later ones. Origin authentication and integrity protection of at least the RTP packet is RECOMMENDED, for example with SRTP (RFC 3711). End-to-end protection prevents a media-aware middlebox (MANE) from doing more than discarding whole packets unless it is a trusted part of the security context.

For congestion control, RTP rules apply. Over best-effort service, senders MUST monitor packet loss, and loss is acceptable if a TCP flow on the same path would get at least the throughput of all the RTP streams combined. For pre-encoded content, the key tool is temporal scalability: a sender can drop NAL units with a high TID.
sections.plainLanguage: Hidden messages inside a video should never be trusted blindly. And the sender should slow down when the network gets crowded, like not hogging a shared road.

fields.name: F
fields.desc: forbidden_zero_bit; required to be zero in HEVC.

fields.desc: nal_unit_type; below 32 means a VCL NAL unit.

fields.name: LayerId
fields.desc: nuh_layer_id; required to be zero in HEVC.

viz.caption: PAYLOAD HEADER TYPE VALUES USED BY THE PAYLOAD FORMAT

items.label: Single NAL unit packet
items.desc: The payload header copies the NAL unit header of the one NAL unit inside.

items.label: Aggregation packet (AP)
items.desc: Two or more NAL units of one access unit.

items.label: Fragmentation unit (FU)
items.desc: A fragment of a single NAL unit.

items.label: PACI packet
items.desc: Carries a payload header extension in front of a NAL unit, FU or AP.

fields.name: S
fields.desc: 1 on the first fragment of a NAL unit.

fields.name: E
fields.desc: 1 on the last fragment of a NAL unit.

fields.name: FuType
fields.desc: Equal to the Type of the fragmented NAL unit.

items.title: SRST
items.text: A single RTP stream on a single media transport.

items.title: MRST
items.text: Multiple RTP streams over a single media transport.

items.title: MRMT
items.text: Multiple RTP streams on multiple media transports; suited to multicast.
